# Proof

**Statement:** In a quadratic number field, any two-generated ideal is a free ℤ-module of rank two.

**The statement is TRUE.**

Let $K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ be a quadratic number field with $d$ a squarefree integer, and let $\mathcal{O}_K$ be its ring of integers.

**Step 1: $\mathcal{O}_K$ is a free ℤ-module of rank 2.**

This is standard. We have $\mathcal{O}_K = \mathbb{Z}[\omega]$ where
$$\omega = \begin{cases} \sqrt{d} & \text{if } d \equiv 2, 3 \pmod{4}, \\ \frac{1+\sqrt{d}}{2} & \text{if } d \equiv 1 \pmod{4}. \end{cases}$$
In either case $\{1, \omega\}$ is a ℤ-basis, so $\mathcal{O}_K \cong \mathbb{Z}^2$ as a ℤ-module.

**Step 2: Every ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ is a free ℤ-module of rank at most 2.**

Any ideal $I \subseteq \mathcal{O}_K$ is a ℤ-submodule of $\mathcal{O}_K \cong \mathbb{Z}^2$. Since $\mathbb{Z}$ is a PID, every submodule of a free ℤ-module of rank $n$ is free of rank $\leq n$. Hence $I$ is free of rank $\leq 2$.

**Step 3: Every *nonzero* ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ has rank exactly 2.**

Let $I \neq 0$ be an ideal. Pick $0 \neq \alpha \in I$. Then
$$\alpha \cdot \mathcal{O}_K \subseteq I \subseteq \mathcal{O}_K.$$

Multiplication by $\alpha$ is an injective ℤ-linear endomorphism of $\mathcal{O}_K \cong \mathbb{Z}^2$ (injective because $\mathcal{O}_K$ is an integral domain), so $\alpha \mathcal{O}_K$ is a full-rank sublattice of $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Therefore $[\mathcal{O}_K : \alpha\mathcal{O}_K] < \infty$. Since $\alpha\mathcal{O}_K \subseteq I \subseteq \mathcal{O}_K$, we have
$$[\mathcal{O}_K : I] \leq [\mathcal{O}_K : \alpha\mathcal{O}_K] < \infty.$$

A subgroup of finite index in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is itself isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^2$ (it has the same rank). Therefore $I \cong \mathbb{Z}^2$, i.e., $I$ is free of rank 2.

**Step 4: A two-generated ideal is nonzero (in the meaningful sense) and hence has rank 2.**

A two-generated ideal $I = (a, b)$ is generated by two elements $a, b \in \mathcal{O}_K$. If at least one of $a, b$ is nonzero, then $I$ is a nonzero ideal, and by Step 3 it is a free ℤ-module of rank 2.

The only degenerate case is $a = b = 0$, giving the zero ideal. But the zero ideal is generated by a single element (or the empty set), so it is not properly "two-generated" in the sense of *requiring* two generators. In standard algebraic number theory, "two-generated ideal" refers to a nonzero ideal generated by two elements. (Indeed, in a Dedekind domain every nonzero ideal is generated by at most two elements, so "two-generated" is the natural class of nonzero ideals.)

**Conclusion:** Every two-generated (nonzero) ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ is a free ℤ-module of rank 2. The statement is **true**. $\blacksquare$
